facts.fact: Consultant Willard Shoko says Liquid Intelligent Technologies operates over 26,000 km of fibre in Zimbabwe as the core long-haul terrestrial routing layer; no places named. Dated by the article (2026-09-12).

Shoko says Powertel and Paratus Zimbabwe formed an equal-investment PPP to build a DWDM fibre backhaul network across Zimbabwe, starting with an active 800 Gbps link between Plumtree and Bulawayo, on Powertel's powerline-based national fibre; no date given, article date used.

Shoko says DFA Zimbabwe built a 1,500 km optical fibre backbone along railway servitudes from Beitbridge through Bulawayo, Harare and Mutare (about $18M+ with BCS Group and Dandemutande); no date given, article date used.
Shoko says the DFA Zimbabwe 1,500 km backbone is open-access and gives local ISPs and mobile operators wholesale backhaul.

systems.owner: DFA Zimbabwe with BCS Group and Dandemutande
